title: Sell Mineral Rights in Rogers, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Rogers, OH | Columbiana County
metaDescription: Own oil and gas or mineral rights near Rogers, Columbiana County? Learn how flank-position Utica interests are valued and how to get a no-pressure cash offer.
heroLead: Rogers sits on the western flank of the Utica/Point Pleasant play, and most of the mineral owners we talk with here inherited a fractional interest from a grandparent's farm rather than negotiated a lease themselves.
intro: Rogers is a small, unincorporated crossroads community in northern Columbiana County, known locally for its weekly outdoor trading post. Underneath the farmland surrounding it, the same Utica/Point Pleasant shale that made Carroll and Harrison Counties famous continues west, but it thins and the gas window gets shallower here than in the core counties to the south. That does not mean interests are worthless; it means the story is different, and it is worth understanding before you decide what to do with a mineral deed you may have never seen.
Most owners we hear from around Rogers hold a small fractional share, an eighth or a sixteenth, split among cousins after a farm was sold generations ago but the minerals were kept.

sections.heading: Why the flank position changes the math
paragraphs: Operators rank acreage by thickness of the Point Pleasant carbonate and by how much liquid-rich gas versus dry gas the rock will produce. Flank counties like Columbiana generally see thinner pay and lower initial rates than core counties such as Carroll or Harrison just to the south, so lease and purchase interest can be slower and more selective here.

That does not remove value. It shifts it toward whether a specific unit near Rogers has already been permitted, drilled, or is included in a pooled unit. A landman or a buyer looking at your parcel will pull that unit data before quoting anything, and you can ask to see the same records.

sections.heading: Fractional interests and old family deeds
paragraphs: Because so much of Columbiana County farmland changed hands in the mid-1900s with minerals reserved out of the sale, a single 80-acre tract can now have a dozen heirs each owning a sliver. If your name is on an old deed alongside siblings or cousins you have not spoken to in years, that is normal, not a dealbreaker.

A title search at the Columbiana County Recorder's office in Lisbon will trace the chain from the original reservation to you. That chain is what any serious buyer needs before making an offer, so getting a copy early saves time later.

sections.heading: What actually determines the offer
paragraphs: Whether the interest is leased or unleased, whether a well is producing on your unit or pooled acreage near it, the royalty rate in the existing lease if one exists, and recent activity trends in Columbiana County all factor into what a buyer will quote. Any number you hear should be tied to those specifics and to recent comparable activity, not a flat promise.

We look at the same public permit and production data the operators use, walk you through what it shows for acreage near Rogers, and put a written, no-obligation offer in front of you so you can compare it against keeping the interest.

faqs.question: Is my mineral interest near Rogers worth anything if there is no well on it yet?
faqs.answer: Often yes, though unleased and undrilled acreage on the flank typically carries less immediate value than a producing tract. Value here depends heavily on whether nearby units have been permitted or pooled, which we check before quoting.

faqs.question: I only own a small fractional share inherited from my grandfather's farm. Can I still sell?
faqs.answer: Yes. Fractional interests, even a sixteenth or smaller, are the most common thing we buy in this part of Columbiana County. You do not need the other heirs to sell your own share.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my Rogers-area parcel is in the Utica core or the flank?
faqs.answer: The Ohio Department of Natural Resources publishes well permit and production maps by township, and we can walk you through what those show for your specific tract.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer to sell mineral rights near Rogers?
faqs.answer: It is not required, but for larger or contested interests many owners choose to have an attorney review the deed before closing. We provide the draft deed early so you or your advisor has time to review it.
